item.title: Trump signals U.S. may leave allies to manage Iran fallout
item.summary: The threat comes as Marines sail toward the region amid widespread speculation that U.S. soldiers could be called on to deploy.

item.summary: Ballard Partners will represent Khalifa Hifter and his armed forces, signaling a renegade commander’s desire to gain influence in Washington.

item.title: Supreme Court to consider whether Trump can end protected status for Syrians, Haitians
item.summary: A decision by the Supreme Court could affect other challenges to the government’s efforts to end temporary protected status for hundreds of thousands of migrants.

item.summary: Groups that include pro-Israel organizations obscured their spending in some midterm races to try to defeat candidates that oppose their cause.

item.title: Trump administration asks Congress to block state limits on AI
item.summary: White House advisers aim to codify policies to protect AI companies’ interests, despite past opposition from many Republican governors and influencers.

item.title: Tracking who Trump is appointing to fill key administration roles
item.summary: Follow President Trump’s progress filling over 800 positions, among about 1,300 that require Senate confirmation, in this tracker from The Washington Post and the Partnership for Public Service.

item.title: Trump continues to target Robert Mueller after his death
item.summary: Mueller, who led the Russia investigation and the bureau after 9/11, remained a target of Trump years after his probe of possible election interference.

item.title: Robert Mueller, ex-FBI director at center of political tempest, dies at 81
item.summary: After building a reputation for quiet rectitude, he became a political target as special counsel investigating Russian interference in the 2016 election.

item.title: Trump threatens to deploy ICE to airports as TSA shortages drive delays
item.summary: Spring break travel is straining airports as rising callouts and resignations among unpaid TSA officers stretch security over a month into the funding standoff.

item.title: Museum that explores how enslaved people were freed sues over grant cancellation
item.summary: The founders of an Underground Railroad history site in Albany, New York, claim the Trump administration’s funding cuts were aimed at marginalizing Black history.
